title: Cap. IX Arg. 7 Sol: why all reprobates become unbelieving — Augustine Ad Simpl.: nothing worse infused; only what would make better is not given; Prosper
pass_a_gloss: But how comes it that all the reprobated always turn out unbelieving and impenitent, if this unbelief and impenitence are not fruits or effects of antecedent reprobation? I answer from Augustine, Ad Simpl. l. 1. qu. 2. Not that by God reprobating anything is inflicted whereby a man is worse, but only that that whereby he would be better is not bestowed. It is not therefore a consequence that God, from whom he has not given penitence, has taken away repentance; and those whom he has not lifted up, he has dashed down, etc. as Prosper excellently, Ad Object. Vinc. Resp. 15. And unto the same sentence elsewhere he answers, Ad cap. Gallor. resp. 14. That the unbelief of those not believing the Gospel is by no means generated from the predestination of God; but that all the non-predestined perish by voluntary, not forced, unbelief, Sentent. super 14.
pass_b_english: But how is it that all the reprobate always turn out unbelieving and impenitent, if that unbelief and impenitence are not fruits or effects of antecedent reprobation? I answer with Augustine (Ad Simpl. 1.2): not that God by reprobating inflicts anything by which a man is made worse, but only that what would make him better is not bestowed. So it does not follow that those to whom God has not given penitence he has robbed of repentance, or that those he has not lifted he has dashed down — as Prosper well says (Ad Object. Vinc. Resp. 15). And elsewhere to the same effect (Ad cap. Gallor. resp. 14): the unbelief of those who do not believe the Gospel is in no way generated from God's predestination; all the non-predestined perish by voluntary, not forced, unbelief (Sentent. super 14).
source_text: Sed qui fit quod omnes reprobati semper evadunt infideles et impoenitentes, si infidelitas haec et impoenitentia non sint fructus aut effecta antecedentis reprobationis? Respondeo ex Augustino, Ad Simpl. l. 1. qu. 2. Non quod a Deo reprobante irrogetur aliquid quo sit homo deterior, sed tantum quod quo sit melior non erogetur. Non est ergo consequens, ut Deus quibus poenitentiam non dederit, resipiscentiam abstulerit; et quos non levaverit, alliserit, etc. ut optime Prosper, Ad Object. Vinc. Resp. 15. Et in eandem sententiam alibi respondet, Ad cap. Gallor. resp. 14. Infidelitatem non credentium Evangelio nequaquam ex Dei praedestinatione generari; sed omnes non-praedestinatos perire infidelitate voluntaria, non coacta, Sentent. super 14.
